suan-hua.title: Acid soil: seedlings stall, root tips go brown
suan-hua.subtitle: pH is a measurement, not a disease. On grain land, consider lime only when pH is below about 5.5.
suan-hua.summary: When seedlings stall and the next ridge stays green, pull one plant and wash the roots. Brown, bald tips mean test plough-layer pH. On grain land, consider lime only below about 5.5.
suan-hua.card: Stunted seedlings: check the root tips, then pH. On grain land, consider lime only below about 5.5.

yan-jian.title: Saline soil: white crust and scorched margins
yan-jian.subtitle: Split salt from alkali. Salt is EC; alkali is pH and sodium.
yan-jian.summary: Crouch and read the surface: a thin white powder, or a crust you can peel. Emergence is patchy, leaf margins scorch. A light watering makes wilt worse — that is not drought. Pull o
yan-jian.card: Split salt from alkali. Salt is EC; alkali is pH and sodium.

ban-jie.title: Hard soil: a shiny pan the roots will not cross
ban-jie.subtitle: After rain a slurry, when dry a cap. Look at twenty centimetres before you feed.
ban-jie.summary: Try the hoe: after rain a slurry, when dry a cap that bounces the blade. Seedlings wear a cap of soil; roots run sideways. Dig a pit in the wheel track and look at about twenty cen
ban-jie.card: After rain a slurry, when dry a cap. Look at twenty centimetres before you feed.

you-ji-zhi.title: Thin organic matter: pale soil that will not hold a ball
you-ji-zhi.subtitle: Organic matter is a reserve, not a packet of microbes. Build it over years.
you-ji-zhi.summary: Rub a handful of plough-layer soil: pale, powdery, it will not hold a ball and runs through the fingers. Fertiliser after one rain looks as if you never applied it. Bare ground in
you-ji-zhi.card: Organic matter is a reserve, not a packet of microbes. Build it over years.

que-dan.title: Nitrogen: old leaves yellow, new leaves still green
que-dan.subtitle: Yellow old leaves, white roots. If new leaves yellow too, think sulphur or iron.
que-dan.summary: Read which leaves are yellow. Old leaves evenly yellow, new leaves still green, and washed roots still white: that looks like nitrogen. If new leaves yellow too, think sulphur or i
que-dan.card: Yellow old leaves, white roots. If new leaves yellow too, think sulphur or iron.

que-jia.title: Potassium: scorch from the old-leaf margin
que-jia.subtitle: Scorched margins plus a white crust: split salt from potassium first.
que-jia.summary: Old-leaf margins scorch first and roll inward; stems soften; fruit is bland. Pick the worst old leaves and see whether the scorch walks in from the edge. The soil surface need not
que-jia.card: Scorched margins plus a white crust: split salt from potassium first.

que-lin.title: Phosphorus shortage: seedlings purple, stiff, short of roots
que-lin.subtitle: Cold and acid soils lock phosphorus even when the bag was applied.
que-lin.summary: Dark green with purple on the underside; roots short. Not the even yellow of nitrogen shortage.

que-tie.title: Iron: new leaves yellow, veins still green
que-tie.subtitle: Often a pH lock, not a missing bag of iron.
que-tie.summary: Decide whether the yellow leaves are new or old. New leaves yellow with veins still green, worse at the tip, while old leaves stay greener: that looks like iron shortage or iron lo
que-tie.card: Often a pH lock, not a missing bag of iron.

que-xin.title: Zinc shortage: new leaves stripe, internodes shrink
que-xin.subtitle: High phosphorus often hides zinc. Look at the newest growth.
que-xin.summary: Interveinal striping on new leaves, shortened internodes, a rosette look. Don’t keep pouring phosphate.

lian-zuo.title: Same-crop fatigue: the same field gets worse each year
lian-zuo.subtitle: A microbe bag has no unit that replaces rotation.
lian-zuo.summary: Same crop, same bed, weaker plants, more wilt. Salt, disease and tired roots arrive together. Rotate, don’t only sterilise.

dashe-yanzhi.title: Greenhouse salt: white frost under the film, the bed gets saltier
dashe-yanzhi.subtitle: The film is an umbrella, not a pickaxe. Salt has nowhere to go.
dashe-yanzhi.summary: White crust at the drip line, leaf edges burn, yield drops. Flush only if you have a way out; don’t just change the soil.

shao-gen.title: Fertiliser burn: a row of scorched seedlings along the band
shao-gen.subtitle: Move the granules, dilute, wait for new roots. Do not add another bag.
shao-gen.summary: Within days of a dressing, leaves scorch and roots blacken in a line along the seed furrow or dripper. Scrape the soil and you see undissolved granules. Compare that row with plant
shao-gen.card: Move the granules, dilute, wait for new roots. Do not add another bag.

lao-hai.title: Waterlogging: wilt by day, wet soil, black roots
lao-hai.subtitle: Drain first. Urea cannot enter a drowned root.
lao-hai.summary: Wilt by day, recover a little at night, standing water or a squelch underfoot, cool subsoil. Pull a plant: white roots or black and smelly. Wet soil that still wilts is not drought
lao-hai.card: Drain first. Urea cannot enter a drowned root.

wei-sheng-wu.title: The soil isn’t ‘alive’: microbes out of balance
wei-sheng-wu.subtitle: A bottle of inoculant is not a substitute for organic matter and air.
wei-sheng-wu.summary: Soil smells sour or dead, residues don’t rot, plants stall. Feed carbon and air before you buy a miracle bottle.

ce-tu-bao-gao.title: Reading a soil-test sheet
ce-tu-bao-gao.subtitle: The sheet is a measurement, not a prescription. Circle pH, organic matter and salt first.
ce-tu-bao-gao.summary: Match the field name, sampling depth and date before you read any number. Order: pH, organic matter, salt or EC, then NPK, then micronutrients. Misread the unit and the fertiliser
ce-tu-bao-gao.card: The sheet is a measurement, not a prescription. Circle pH, organic matter and salt first.

ce-tu-qu-yang.title: Sampling for a soil test: how to miss the truth
ce-tu-qu-yang.subtitle: One spadeful from the ditch bank is not this field.
ce-tu-qu-yang.summary: Mix 8–15 spots of the tilled layer. Skip the headland, the manure heap and the wet corner. Depth is part of the number.

que-gai.title: Calcium shortage: dead tips, blossom-end rot, split fruit
que-gai.subtitle: Calcium in the soil is not calcium in the fruit. Water flow carries it.
que-gai.summary: Growing tips die, fruit pits rot at the blossom end, shells split. Don’t only spray the leaf; check water and pH.

que-mei.title: Magnesium shortage: old leaves yellow between still-green veins
que-mei.subtitle: Old leaves, not new ones. Don’t mix with iron.
que-mei.summary: Interveinal yellow on older leaves. High potassium or acid soil often sits behind it.

que-peng.title: Boron shortage: flowers without fruit, cracked stems, hollow hearts
que-peng.subtitle: Deficiency and toxicity are a thin sheet of paper apart.
que-peng.summary: Flowers drop, hearts go hollow, growing points die. Drought and salt can look the same. Don’t double the dose.

que-meng.title: Manganese shortage: new leaves speckle between the veins
que-meng.subtitle: High pH locks manganese the way it locks iron.
que-meng.summary: New leaves pale with brown specks between veins. Not the even yellow of nitrogen.

que-liu.title: Sulfur shortage: the whole plant yellows, including new leaves
que-liu.subtitle: Unlike nitrogen, the new growth yellows too.
que-liu.summary: Even yellow on new and old leaves. Sandy, low-organic soils after heavy rain show it first.

que-tong.title: Copper shortage: empty heads, bleached leaf tips
que-tong.subtitle: A trace. Doubling it hurts.
que-tong.summary: Grain doesn’t fill, tips bleach. Organic soils and high pH make it worse.

que-mu.title: Molybdenum shortage: legumes fail to fix nitrogen, leaves twist
que-mu.subtitle: Acid soils lock molybdenum. Lime sometimes unlocks it.
que-mu.summary: Pale, twisted leaves on beans; nodules fail. Don’t pour nitrogen before you check pH.

yang-fen-kang-kang.title: Nutrients fighting each other: phosphorus vs zinc, potassium vs magnesium
yang-fen-kang-kang.subtitle: More of one bag can starve another.
yang-fen-kang-kang.summary: A high-P dressing hides zinc. Heavy K hides magnesium. Read the sheet, don’t stack the same salt.

yao-hai.title: Spray injury: spots and twists after the tank, not a slow shortage
yao-hai.subtitle: It arrives in hours or a day, not over a week of yellowing.
yao-hai.summary: Speckles, puckered leaves, dead spots after a spray. Pattern follows the boom. Don’t treat it as a nutrient gap.

miao-qi-fei-hai.title: Seedling fertiliser burn: they come up already scorching
miao-qi-fei-hai.subtitle: Black root tips at emergence are a burn, not ‘not enough food’.
miao-qi-fei-hai.summary: Emergence is patchy, tips black, stems watery. Water and wait. Don’t add another dressing.

an-hai.title: Ammonia burn: the dressing fumes the leaves the same day
an-hai.subtitle: Urea or ammonium on wet heat can gas the crop.
an-hai.summary: Leaf tips bleach and smell of ammonia after a surface dressing. Water in, don’t cover with more N.

lv-hai.title: Chloride injury: a chloride-shy crop meets a chloride fertiliser
lv-hai.subtitle: Potato, tobacco, some fruit — chloride is not a free ride.
lv-hai.summary: Leaf margins burn on chloride-sensitive crops after KCl. Switch the potassium source, don’t just cut the rate blindly.

di-guan-nong-du.title: Drip too strong: every watering can salt the root zone
di-guan-nong-du.subtitle: EC over the line is a brine, not a feed.
di-guan-nong-du.summary: Tips burn, white at the emitter, growth stalls. Dilute, flush if you can drain, then restart weaker.

wei-fu-shu-you-ji-fei.title: Raw manure: you thought it was treasure, it burned the seedlings
wei-fu-shu-you-ji-fei.subtitle: Heat, salt and ammonia from unfinished compost.
wei-fu-shu-you-ji-fei.summary: Hot piles, white fungus, burned roots after a ‘organic’ dressing. Only fully rotted stuff goes next to a seedling.

fan-yan.title: Salt rising: after you water, the soil is whiter
fan-yan.subtitle: Water that can’t leave brings the salt back up.
fan-yan.summary: A white film after irrigation and sun. Cover and drain. Don’t flood without an outlet.

shi-hui-xing-tu.title: Calcareous soil: the fertiliser is in the ground, the root can’t eat it
shi-hui-xing-tu.subtitle: High pH locks iron, zinc and phosphorus.
shi-hui-xing-tu.summary: New leaves yellow with green veins, P stays purple. Don’t keep pouring the same bag. Work the root zone.

shi-gao-gai-jian.title: Gypsum for alkali, leaching for salt — they are not the same job
shi-gao-gai-jian.subtitle: White crust is salt. Slick hard cap is more sodium.
shi-gao-gai-jian.summary: Gypsum helps sodic soil. Salt still needs water that can leave. Don’t spread gypsum on every white film.

sha-tu-lou-fei.title: Sandy soil leaks water and fertiliser
sha-tu-lou-fei.subtitle: Little and often. Don’t dump a season in one pile.
sha-tu-lou-fei.summary: Colour pales, fertiliser is gone after rain. Organic matter in small repeated doses, split nitrogen.

nian-tu-nan-geng.title: Clay that won’t till, then cracks
nian-tu-nan-geng.subtitle: Work it at the right moisture or you forge a brick.
nian-tu-nan-geng.summary: Sticky when wet, plates when dry. Organic matter and the right window beat adding sand.

li-di-ceng.title: The plough pan: a lid under the rotary tiller
li-di-ceng.subtitle: The hoe works the top, roots hit a floor.
li-di-ceng.summary: A dense smear at tillage depth. Subsoil only when dry enough to crack. Don’t go deeper than the pan.

hei-tu-tui-hua.title: Black soil getting thin and hard
hei-tu-tui-hua.subtitle: Northeast chernozem is not an endless warehouse.
hei-tu-tui-hua.summary: Colour fades, clods increase, organic matter drops. Return straw, cut the years of only taking.

jie-gan-huan-tian.title: Straw return: it can feed the soil and also burn or steal nitrogen
jie-gan-huan-tian.subtitle: Carbon without extra nitrogen is a tug-of-war at the seedling.
jie-gan-huan-tian.summary: Yellow seedlings after a heavy straw layer. Chop, mix, add a little N, don’t bury a wet mat.

shi-hui-yong-liang.title: Agricultural lime: how much, and when
shi-hui-yong-liang.subtitle: Farm lime 50–150 kg/mu (about 750–2250 kg/ha), split, sandy soils low. No builder’s lime.
shi-hui-yong-liang.summary: Open this page only after you have decided to amend acid soil. Read the bag: agricultural lime can go on the field; builder’s lime and leftover renovation lime cannot. Match textur
shi-hui-yong-liang.card: Farm lime 50–150 kg/mu (about 750–2250 kg/ha), split, sandy soils low. No builder’s lime.

xiu-shui-tian.title: Rusty-water paddies: ferrous iron poisoning
xiu-shui-tian.subtitle: An oil film and rusty water are not a nitrogen shortage.
xiu-shui-tian.summary: Seedlings yellow and stiff, roots coated rust, an oil film on the water. Drain and air, don’t chase N.

qian-yu-tian.title: Cold waterlogged fields, gleying: soil is cold, roots don’t grow
qian-yu-tian.subtitle: Blue-grey soil and standing water. That’s gleying, not ‘needs more urea’.
qian-yu-tian.summary: Soil stays cold and grey-blue, roots few. Raise the bed, drain, wait for warmth.

shui-tian-huan-yuan.title: Paddy reduction: black, smelly roots, no new white tips
shui-tian-huan-yuan.subtitle: No air in the mud. Fertiliser can’t fix a drowned root.
shui-tian-huan-yuan.summary: Roots black, a rotten smell, no new white tips. Mid-season drain, then shallow water.

gen-fu-jian-bie.title: Root rot or a soil problem: look at the root before you fertilise
gen-fu-jian-bie.subtitle: A brown bald tip from acid is not the same as a wet rot.
gen-fu-jian-bie.summary: Wash the root. Acid aluminium is brown and bald. Rot is soft and smells. Disease follows the stem.

huang-ye-jian-bie.title: Yellow leaves: shortage, waterlog, spray injury or disease
huang-ye-jian-bie.subtitle: Which leaf yellows first tells you more than the colour.
huang-ye-jian-bie.summary: Old leaf vs new leaf, veins vs blade, a spray pattern vs a slow fade. Separate them before you open a bag.

han-yan-jian-bie.title: Drought or salt: how to tell a wilt from a scorched edge
han-yan-jian-bie.subtitle: Salt wilt can look like thirst and then get worse when you water.
han-yan-jian-bie.summary: Dry soil plus recovery at night leans drought. White crust plus worse after watering leans salt.

cha-yuan-guo-suan.title: Tea gardens too acid: tolerant is not ‘the more acid the better’
cha-yuan-guo-suan.subtitle: Don’t push tea to neutrality; don’t treat tea like grain.
cha-yuan-guo-suan.summary: Tea likes acid, not a dead root from aluminium. Grain lime rates will hurt the bush.

ma-ling-shu-tu.title: Potato scab and a soil that leans alkaline
ma-ling-shu-tu.subtitle: Scab likes a higher pH. Don’t lime a potato ground by habit.
ma-ling-shu-tu.summary: Russet scab on tubers in high-pH, dry soils. Keep pH in the potato window, irrigate at tuber set.

sheng-wu-you-ji-fei.title: Bio-organic fertiliser: how to use it so it isn’t a placebo
sheng-wu-you-ji-fei.subtitle: Look at composting, salt and the C:N, not the cartoon on the bag.
sheng-wu-you-ji-fei.summary: A live inoculant on dead, salty, raw compost does nothing. Buy rotted material first.

guo-yuan-tu-rang.title: Orchard soil: how to feed the layer under the tree
guo-yuan-tu-rang.subtitle: The drip line is where the feeder roots are.
guo-yuan-tu-rang.summary: Don’t dump everything at the trunk. Organic matter, a living cover, and a test beat a yearly dump.

da-peng-lian-zuo-zong-he.title: Greenhouse decline: salt, disease and burn arriving together
da-peng-lian-zuo-zong-he.subtitle: One sterilisation is not a rotation.
da-peng-lian-zuo-zong-he.summary: White crust, wilt, burn after a rich year. Flush, rotate, rest the bed. Don’t only change the soil.

hong-huang-rang-gai-suan.title: Red-yellow earth: test pH before you consider lime
hong-huang-rang-gai-suan.subtitle: Southern red soil is acid by nature. Don’t copy a northern lime bill.
hong-huang-rang-gai-suan.summary: Stiff seedlings, rusty water, red or yellow clay. Lime only below about 5.5, split, sandy soils low.

lv-du-shang-gen.title: Aluminium injury: brown, bald root tips
lv-du-shang-gen.subtitle: On grain land, consider lime only below about 5.5. Do not push urea onto bald tips.
lv-du-shang-gen.summary: Washed tips are brown and bald, with few laterals. More nitrogen will not make a canopy. Pull one stalled plant, rinse, and look for remaining white points. A starved root is still
lv-du-shang-gen.card: On grain land, consider lime only below about 5.5. Do not push urea onto bald tips.

suan-yu-que-gai.title: Acid soil and calcium shortage together: blossom-end rot is not only a foliar calcium job
suan-yu-que-gai.subtitle: If the root is being bitten, spraying the fruit is a delay.
suan-yu-que-gai.summary: Acid locks calcium and aluminium bites the tip. Test pH, then talk calcium.

suan-tu-shi-lin.title: Acid soil locks phosphorus: purple, dwarf seedlings — fix acid before you pour more P
suan-tu-shi-lin.subtitle: Iron and aluminium grab phosphate in acid ground.
suan-tu-shi-lin.summary: Purple stiff seedlings on acid fields. A band of P plus lime beats another broadcast of the same bag.

sheng-li-suan-xing-fei.title: Physiological acid fertilisers make the soil more acid year after year
sheng-li-suan-xing-fei.subtitle: Ammonium-N is a bill the soil pays in pH.
sheng-li-suan-xing-fei.summary: Years of ammonium without a pH reading. Rotate the N source, retest.

cha-yuan-shi-hui-jin-ji.title: Lime taboos in tea: how to correct acid without hurting the bush
cha-yuan-shi-hui-jin-ji.subtitle: Don’t push tea to neutrality.
cha-yuan-shi-hui-jin-ji.summary: Tea wants acid. Grain lime rates overshoot. Small doses, far from the collar, retest.

su-da-yan-jian.title: Soda saline-alkali: alkali and salt are not the same thing
su-da-yan-jian.subtitle: Slick, hard, high pH is sodium. White powder is salt.
su-da-yan-jian.summary: Don’t spread gypsum on every white film, and don’t leach a sodic cap the same way you wash table salt.

bin-hai-yan-tu.title: Coastal saline soil: drain and wash first, then talk fertility
bin-hai-yan-tu.subtitle: A fertile dressing on undrained salt is a waste.
bin-hai-yan-tu.summary: White crust near the sea, poor emergence. Ditches that actually empty, then organic matter.

wei-xian-shui-guan-gai.title: Slightly saline irrigation: you can water, you cannot water the same way every time
wei-xian-shui-guan-gai.subtitle: The salt in the well is a bill.
wei-xian-shui-guan-gai.summary: Alternate with fresher water if you have it, leach when you can drain, watch EC.

di-biao-fu-yan.title: Salt rising at the mulch edge: white frost along the film
di-biao-fu-yan.subtitle: The film is an umbrella, not a pickaxe.
di-biao-fu-yan.summary: White at the hole and the edge. Don’t just punch more holes. Manage water under the sheet.

yan-jian-di-xuan-zuo.title: What to plant on saline-alkali land: keep the seedling alive before you chase yield
yan-jian-di-xuan-zuo.subtitle: A crop that comes up is worth more than a high-yield variety that dies.
yan-jian-di-xuan-zuo.summary: Match salt tolerance, plant on ridges, don’t start with the thirstiest crop.

xi-yan-pai-shui.title: Leaching salt: irrigation without drainage just drives the salt up
xi-yan-pai-shui.subtitle: A flush needs a way out.
xi-yan-pai-shui.summary: Open the drain, then water. Cover to stop the return. Don’t flood a closed basin.

da-peng-huan-tu-xi-yan.title: Replace the greenhouse soil or wash it: don’t strip the shed at the first white crust
da-peng-huan-tu-xi-yan.subtitle: Washing with a drain is cheaper than a truck of new soil — if the salt can leave.
da-peng-huan-tu-xi-yan.summary: Test EC. If you can drain, wash. If the film has trapped years of drip salt, then talk replacement.

xuan-geng-bian-qian.title: Rotary tillage every year: the tilled layer gets shallower
xuan-geng-bian-qian.subtitle: The rotor makes a floor.
xuan-geng-bian-qian.summary: A fluffy top and a pan underneath. Change depth, subsoil in the dry window, don’t only spin faster.

shen-song-shi-ji.title: The subsoiling window: when and how deep
shen-song-shi-ji.subtitle: Dry enough to crack, only just below the pan.
shen-song-shi-ji.summary: A wet subsoiler smears a new lid. Find the pan with a spade, set the leg there, protect the cracks.

tu-rang-tuan-ju-ti.title: Aggregates smashed: the surface powders, then turns to slurry in rain
tu-rang-tuan-ju-ti.subtitle: A stable crumb is built, not bought in one bag.
tu-rang-tuan-ju-ti.summary: Dust when dry, soup when wet. Organic matter, roots and fewer passes.

ji-ya-che-zhe.title: Wheel tracks: seedlings don’t come up in the rut
ji-ya-che-zhe.subtitle: One wet pass packs more than a dry season of work.
ji-ya-che-zhe.summary: Ruts hold water and starve air. Stay off wet ground, use the same tracks.

ban-jie-yu-gen-xi.title: Hard soil and shallow roots feed each other
ban-jie-yu-gen-xi.subtitle: A shallow root can’t break a pan; a pan keeps the root shallow.
ban-jie-yu-gen-xi.summary: Break the lid in the dry window, then keep living roots in the ground.

fu-gai-gai-zhi-di.title: Can film or straw mulch loosen hard soil
fu-gai-gai-zhi-di.subtitle: Mulch is an umbrella for raindrop smash, not a plough.
fu-gai-gai-zhi-di.summary: It stops the cap forming. It does not replace a cracked pan underneath.

lv-fei-fan-ya.title: Green manure: it can feed the soil and also smother the next crop
lv-fei-fan-ya.subtitle: Turn it in with time to rot, not the week you plant.
lv-fei-fan-ya.summary: A wet mat steals nitrogen and air. Chop, wait for white mould, then plant.

sheng-wu-tan.title: Biochar: scattering a little per mu is not a turnaround
sheng-wu-tan.subtitle: Charge it, mix it, don’t treat it as lime or fertiliser.
sheng-wu-tan.summary: Raw char can lock nitrogen. It is not a pH recipe and not a yield button.

you-ji-fei-ru-he-xuan.title: Choosing organic fertiliser: look at composting, salt and the C:N ratio
you-ji-fei-ru-he-xuan.subtitle: The cartoon on the bag is not a test.
you-ji-fei-ru-he-xuan.summary: Smell, heat, EC and a C:N you can live with. Raw, salty, high-N waste burns.

jie-gan-bu-dan.title: The nitrogen bill when you return straw
jie-gan-bu-dan.subtitle: Carbon without a little N is a tug-of-war at the seedling.
jie-gan-bu-dan.summary: A rough field rate is extra N with the straw, not a second full dressing later when the crop is already yellow.

hei-tu-you-ji-zhi-shou-hu.title: Black-soil organic matter drops fast — how to keep it
hei-tu-you-ji-zhi-shou-hu.subtitle: Stop mining the warehouse.
hei-tu-you-ji-zhi-shou-hu.summary: Return straw, cover, cut bare winter. A number on the sheet is a trend, not a one-year panic.

sha-tu-zeng-you-ji-zhi.title: Building organic matter on sand: little and often, not one mountain
sha-tu-zeng-you-ji-zhi.subtitle: A dump of manure on sand salts and then disappears.
sha-tu-zeng-you-ji-zhi.summary: Repeated modest dressings, cover crops, don’t pile a year’s waste in August.

que-xin-yu-lin.title: Zinc shortage often hides behind high phosphorus
que-xin-yu-lin.subtitle: The P bag can starve zinc.
que-xin-yu-lin.summary: Striped new leaves after heavy phosphate. Stop stacking P, check zinc.

que-peng-hua-er-bu-shi.title: Flowers without fruit: check boron, also check drought and salt
que-peng-hua-er-bu-shi.subtitle: Empty flowers are not always a boron bottle.
que-peng-hua-er-bu-shi.summary: Look at water and EC first. If boron is low, use a small dose — toxicity is close.

qi-zi-huang-hua.title: Citrus yellowing: separate iron lock, root rot and huanglongbing
qi-zi-huang-hua.subtitle: New-leaf yellow with green veins is not the same as a blotchy infected leaf.
qi-zi-huang-hua.summary: Look at the root, the pattern, and whether a neighbour tree matches. Don’t only spray iron.

pu-tao-shi-hui-tu-que-tie.title: Grapes on limey soil: iron is there, the root can’t eat it
pu-tao-shi-hui-tu-que-tie.subtitle: High pH locks iron. Pouring more iron into the bulk soil often fails.
pu-tao-shi-hui-tu-que-tie.summary: New leaves yellow, veins green, on calcareous ground. Work the root zone, not only a foliar panic.

hua-sheng-kong-jia.title: Empty peanut pods: calcium in the soil doesn’t walk into the peg
hua-sheng-kong-jia.subtitle: The peg drinks calcium from the podding layer, not from a deep band.
hua-sheng-kong-jia.summary: Empty shells on dry, acid or calcium-poor pegging soil. Gypsum in the pegging zone, keep that layer moist.

ye-cai-xiao-xing-yuan-su.title: Leafy-veg micronutrients: a foliar spray is not a substitute for fixing the soil
ye-cai-xiao-xing-yuan-su.subtitle: A yellow new leaf can be iron, manganese or a drowned root.
ye-cai-xiao-xing-yuan-su.summary: Spray can buy days. pH, water and organic matter decide whether it comes back.

shui-dao-jiang-miao.title: Rice seedlings stall: acid, cold, toxins, burn — separate them
shui-dao-jiang-miao.subtitle: A stalled rice seedling is not always ‘needs more urea’.
shui-dao-jiang-miao.summary: Wash the root, smell the mud, read pH. Rusty water, black roots, burned tips and cold mud are different jobs.

yu-mi-miao-huang.title: Yellow maize seedlings: nitrogen, zinc, herbicide, waterlog — pick one
yu-mi-miao-huang.subtitle: Old-leaf yellow, new-leaf stripe, a spray pattern, or wilt by day.
yu-mi-miao-huang.summary: Don’t open the nitrogen bag until you know which yellow you have.

gen-jie-xian-chong.title: Root-knot nematodes: galls on the root, extra fertiliser won’t grow it
gen-jie-xian-chong.subtitle: Look at the root. Beads and knots are not fertiliser burn.
gen-jie-xian-chong.summary: Stunted plants with galled roots. Rotation and resistant stock beat another NPK bag.

tu-chuan-ku-wei.title: Soil-borne wilt: look at the vascular brown before you fertilise
tu-chuan-ku-wei.subtitle: A cut stem that is brown inside is not a shortage.
tu-chuan-ku-wei.summary: One plant wilts in the heat, recovers a little at night, neighbours still green. Cut the stem.

qing-ku-bing-tu.title: Bacterial wilt soil: a hot-tent is not a magic wand
qing-ku-bing-tu.subtitle: Heat can knock it back and also cook the structure.
qing-ku-bing-tu.summary: Use it in the window, then rest and rotate. Don’t tent and replant the same host.

cao-mei-lian-zuo.title: Strawberry replant: salt, nematodes and wilt in the same bed
cao-mei-lian-zuo.subtitle: A new variety in old soil is still old soil.
cao-mei-lian-zuo.summary: Clean stock, rotation, salt check. A disinfectant is not a full answer.

ping-guo-zai-zhi.title: Apple replant: the old pit is still the old soil
ping-guo-zai-zhi.subtitle: Digging out the tree doesn’t dig out the fatigue.
ping-guo-zai-zhi.summary: New trees in old holes stall. Move the row, replace the pit, don’t only add a microbe bag.

gao-wen-men-peng.title: Solarisation: it can knock pathogens back and also hurt roots and structure
gao-wen-men-peng.subtitle: A closed film in high sun is a tool with a back edge.
gao-wen-men-peng.summary: Use it on a wet soil in the heat, then rest. Don’t plant into cooked, salty dust the next day.

han-lao-ji-zhuan.title: Drought flipping to flood: the root is hurt before the leaf yellows
han-lao-ji-zhuan.subtitle: A drowned-then-baked root looks like a shortage a week later.
han-lao-ji-zhuan.summary: Wait for new white roots before a full dressing.

di-xia-shui-wei-gao.title: A high water table: the soil never dries, the root never goes deep
di-xia-shui-wei-gao.subtitle: That is a drainage job, not a fertiliser job.
di-xia-shui-wei-gao.summary: Raise the bed, cut a drain that actually empties.

yu-hou-ban-jie-kai-lie.title: After rain the surface caps and cracks: water runs off, seedlings stick
yu-hou-ban-jie-kai-lie.subtitle: A raindrop smash plus no cover.
yu-hou-ban-jie-kai-lie.summary: A light hoe when it can crumble, mulch, organic matter. Don’t pulverise wet.

leng-shui-guan-miao.title: Cold water on seedlings: a stalled paddy is not always hungry
leng-shui-guan-miao.subtitle: Deep cold water holds the root in a fridge.
leng-shui-guan-miao.summary: Shallow, warmer water, then add fertiliser.

yan-jiang-qi-hou-tu.title: River-wetland soils: gleying is meaner than the surface looks
yan-jiang-qi-hou-tu.subtitle: Blue-grey below a green top.
yan-jiang-qi-hou-tu.summary: Drain, ridge, don’t assume a dark colour is fertility.

shui-fei-yi-ti-hua-ec.title: Fertigation: when EC is over the line you are pickling the root
shui-fei-yi-ti-hua-ec.subtitle: The meter at the tail of the drip is part of the recipe.
shui-fei-yi-ti-hua-ec.summary: Read EC, dilute, flush if you can drain. Don’t turn the tap stronger because the leaf is pale.

ji-zhi-yu-tu-rang.title: Substrate and soil are not the same recipe
ji-zhi-yu-tu-rang.subtitle: Coconut coir is not a field. Don’t copy the field bag into a bag of media.
ji-zhi-yu-tu-rang.summary: EC and water in a pot move faster. Recipes from the field burn a tray.

tu-rang-xiao-du-bian-jie.title: The boundary of soil disinfection: after you kill, you have to feed
tu-rang-xiao-du-bian-jie.subtitle: A sterile bed is not a living bed. Don’t tent and replant the same crop as a habit.
tu-rang-xiao-du-bian-jie.summary: Disinfect, then organic matter and a rotation. Another dose next year is a treadmill.

jian-yi-ph-ec.title: pH paper and a conductivity meter at the field edge
jian-yi-ph-ec.subtitle: A meter in the pocket is not a lab, but it beats guessing.
jian-yi-ph-ec.summary: Same water ratio, same depth. Don’t compare your strip to the neighbour’s lab sheet as if they were one number.

shi-fei-tiao-tu-rang.title: Leaves can hint at a fertiliser, they cannot replace a soil test
shi-fei-tiao-tu-rang.subtitle: A yellow leaf has several authors.
shi-fei-tiao-tu-rang.summary: Use the leaf as a clue, then test. Don’t write a season’s recipe from one colour.

nan-fang-shui-tian-yang-fen.title: Southern paddy nutrients: the reduced layer locks what you applied
nan-fang-shui-tian-yang-fen.subtitle: Black mud is not a warehouse you can keep stacking.
nan-fang-shui-tian-yang-fen.summary: Mid-season drain, place fertiliser where a root with air can reach it.
